results.claim: Exact harmonic duality gives a polynomial bound on fixed-width boundary signatures.
results.proof_sketch: Let T be r absorbing terminals and let N be the number of nonterminals. For t∈T, let h_t(v) be the probability that the uniform random walk is absorbed at t, and put g_t(v)=h_t(v)−h_t(s_0(v)). Harmonicity gives h_t(v)−h_t(s_1(v))=−g_t(v). For switching flows x,y with the same supply φ, write d_x(v)=x(v,s_0(v))−x(v,s_1(v)). Regrouping the weighted sum Σ_(u,v)(y−x)(u,v)(h_t(u)−h_t(v)) first by vertices and then by outgoing pairs proves x^−(t)−y^−(t)=Σ_v(d_y(v)−d_x(v))g_t(v). Hence every terminal coordinate differs by at most Σ_v|g_t(v)|≤N/2. Total terminal inflow is fixed at Σ_vφ(v); consequently, if terminal inflows are integral, at most (⌊N/2⌋+1)^(r−1) distinct terminal-inflow vectors are possible for fixed φ. This is polynomial for fixed r. Moreover, for φ≡1 every prescribed d∈[0,1]^N is realizable: solve t_v=1+Σ_{u:s_0(u)=v}(t_u+d_u)/2+Σ_{u:s_1(u)=v}(t_u−d_u)/2. Iteration from t≡1 stays at least 1 and converges because the nonterminal transition matrix is transient. The resulting edge flows are nonnegative. Thus, for two terminals the maximum possible difference is exactly Σ_v|g(v)|, obtained by choosing d_y−d_x=sign(g).

results.claim: A general range bound survives at arbitrary level width, but it can grow linearly with the number of levels.
results.proof_sketch: Let m_i and M_i be the minimum and maximum zero-player hitting probabilities on L_i, and W_i=M_i−m_i. A walk starting at any level at least i must hit L_{i−1} before reaching a sink. The strong Markov property therefore expresses its hitting probability as a convex combination of the values on L_{i−1}. Hence m_{i−1}≤m_i≤M_i≤M_{i−1}. Both successors of v∈L_i have level at least i−1, so |g(v)|=|h(s_0(v))−h(s_1(v))|/2≤W_{i−1}/2. For r vertices per positive level, Σ_v|g(v)|≤(r/2)Σ_i W_{i−1}. This precisely reduces harmonic-flow stability to controlling the cumulative nested level ranges, but does not give a constant bound.

results.claim: For width three, the gap mass and same-supply switching-flow diameter are unbounded; the width-two stability lemma fails already with two positive levels.
results.proof_sketch: For k≥2 set L_i={a_i,b_i,c_i}, with a_0=0 and b_0=1. For i<k use edges a_i→(a_{i−1},a_{i+1}), b_i→(b_{i−1},b_{i+1}), and c_i→(a_{i−1},b_{i−1}). At level k use a_k→(a_{k−1},c_{k−1}), b_k→(b_{k−1},c_{k−1}), and c_k→(a_{k−1},b_{k−1}); the first edge is even. These are exactly the positive levelsets because every edge decreases distance by at most one and each vertex has a forward edge. Direct substitution gives h(a_i)=i/[2(k+1)], h(b_i)=1−i/[2(k+1)], and h(c_i)=1/2. Thus Σ|g|=k(k+7)/[4(k+1)]=Θ(k). By harmonic duality, two switching flows with common supply φ≡1 have sink-1 inflows differing by exactly this amount. For k=2 an explicit certificate, listing (even,odd), is x: a1 (4/3,4/3), b1 (2,1), c1 (4/3,4/3), a2 (7/6,7/6), b2 (3/2,1/2), c2 (1/2,1/2); and y: a1 (7/3,4/3), b1 (1,1), c1 (11/6,5/6), a2 (5/3,2/3), b2 (1,1), c2 (1,0). Every nonsink has net outflow 1, while the sink-1 inflows are 10/3 and 11/6, differing by 3/2>1. For any fixed r>3, add r−3 vertices per level with successors (a_{i−1},b_{i−1}); the obstruction remains and the gap mass becomes k[4+(r−2)(k+3)]/[4(k+1)].

results.claim: Within-level hitting-probability order is not locally determined at width three.
results.proof_sketch: Take L_1={a,b,c}, L_2={X,Y,Z}, with common edges a→(0,X), b→(0,Y), c→(0,1), and Z→(a,c). In completion A let X→(c,b) and Y→(a,b). Harmonicity gives h(c)=1/2, h(a)=h(X)/2, h(b)=h(Y)/2, hence h(a)=3/22>1/22=h(b). In completion B instead let X→(a,b) and Y→(c,a). The same equations now give h(a)=1/22<3/22=h(b). Both graphs are simple, have exactly three vertices in each positive level, and agree on the sinks and every outgoing edge from L_1. Thus the width-two procedure that orders a new level using only the preceding order and the current vertices' outgoing edges has no width-three analogue of that local form.

results.claim: For fixed supply and a fixed number of terminals, all feasible integral boundary signatures of real switching flows can be enumerated in polynomial time.
results.proof_sketch: Consider the rational polyhedron of real switching flows for the given supply φ. If it is nonempty, optimize each of the first r−1 terminal inflows by two linear programs, obtaining extrema α_t and β_t. Harmonic duality applies to every pair of feasible flows, so β_t−α_t≤N/2. Enumerate the integers q_t∈[⌈α_t⌉,⌊β_t⌋] for those r−1 terminals; there are at most (⌊N/2⌋+1)^(r−1) tuples. The final coordinate is forced by Σ_tq_t=Σ_vφ(v). For each tuple, one further rational LP with the terminal-inflow equalities tests realizability. Thus all and only the integral boundary signatures of real switching flows are returned in polynomial time when r is fixed. This does not assert edge integrality.

results.claim: At positive-level width three, one fixed integer supply can admit Θ(N) distinct integral sink-inflow signatures among real switching flows.
results.proof_sketch: In the k-level width-three family, N=3k and the two common-supply flows supplied by harmonic duality have sink-1 inflows separated by D=k(k+7)/[4(k+1)]=Θ(k). The switching-flow feasible region is convex because all conservation constraints are linear and each imbalance lies in [0,1]. Hence convex combinations of the two flows attain every sink-1 inflow in the intervening real interval. That interval contains at least ⌊D⌋=Θ(k)=Θ(N) integers. Since total terminal inflow is N under φ≡1, each such integer gives an integral two-sink signature. Claim 0 supplies the matching O(N) upper bound.

results.claim: For every fixed positive-level width r≥3 and every k≥2, an instance with N=rk nonterminals, hence M=rk+2 total vertices, can have at least 2^(k−1)=2^(N/r−1)=2^((M−2)/r−1) distinct integral switching flows from one origin to the same sink.
results.proof_sketch: Let L_i={a_i,b_i,c_i} and set a_0=1, with origin a_k. For every i put s_0(a_i)=a_{i−1}; put s_1(a_i)=b_{i+1} when i<k and s_1(a_k)=b_k. For i≥2 put (s_0(b_i),s_1(b_i))=(a_{i−1},c_{i−1}) and (s_0(c_i),s_1(c_i))=(b_{i−1},c_{i−1}); give b_1 and c_1 the two distinct sinks as successors. Each vertex has a successor in L_{i−1}, and no edge skips below L_{i−1}, so these are exactly the distance levels. For q∈{0,1}^{k−1}, send one unit on every a_i→a_{i−1}, and q_i units on both a_i→b_{i+1} and b_{i+1}→a_i; all other values are zero. Conservation holds, the origin has net outflow one, and every even-minus-odd difference is one of 0, q_i, or 1−q_i. The sole terminal inflow is one at sink 1. Distinct q give distinct integral flows. For r>3, add r−3 zero-flow vertices per level, each with two distinct forward successors. This repairs the audited counting error: N counts nonterminals, while the ordinary total-vertex count is M=N+2.

results.claim: The exponential multiplicity persists among prefix assignments with an identical external interface, giving a precise obstruction to literal enumeration but not to compression.
results.proof_sketch: For k≥3 take the prefix P=L_1∪⋯∪L_{k−1} in the preceding construction and fix q_{k−1}=0. Varying q_1,…,q_{k−2} produces 2^(k−2) distinct restrictions to edges whose tails lie in P. Nevertheless, every edge crossing between P and L_k has the same flow in all these restrictions: a_k→a_{k−1} carries one and all other crossing edges carry zero. Both sink inflows are also fixed. Thus an algorithm that materializes every integral prefix realization separately has exponential output even after the full cut interface is fixed. Conversely, this same-interface property makes clear that these histories can be merged; it supplies no lower bound against an interface quotient, canonical representative, or other compressed decision algorithm.

results.claim: The obstruction and counterexamples do not resolve polynomial-time ARRIVAL at width three or at any fixed width r>2.
results.proof_sketch: Claims 2 and 3 refute two width-two structural mechanisms, while claims 6 and 7 impose an exponential output lower bound only on explicit certificate or prefix-assignment enumeration. Claim 4 gives polynomially many boundary signatures only after the entire supply vector is fixed. None of these statements bounds the number of relevant varying-supply states, constructs a polynomial-size quotient, proves a polynomial-time decision procedure, or establishes a contrary complexity classification. Therefore the audit's VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS judgment remains the strongest justified target conclusion.

final_writeup:
Here “width r” is interpreted as requiring r vertices in every positive level L_i, i≥1, because L_0 always consists of the two sinks. Exploiting the literal L_0 mismatch would not address the intended open target.

The target remains unresolved. The six audit-verified inherited claims are retained exactly. They give a polynomial bound on boundary signatures for a fixed supply, show that this bound can genuinely grow linearly at width three, and refute two mechanisms supporting the width-two algorithm: constant switching-flow diameter and locally determined hitting-probability order.

The audited refutation concerned the exponential-family vertex count, not the construction itself. The corrected statement distinguishes N=rk nonterminals from M=N+2 total vertices. For every fixed r≥3 and k≥2, the construction has at least 2^(k−1)=2^(N/r−1)=2^((M−2)/r−1) distinct integral switching flows from a single origin to sink 1. In the boundary case r=3,k=2, this means six nonterminals, eight total vertices, and exactly two displayed flows; it no longer incorrectly demands at least four.

Applying the obstruction lens further gives a sharper necessary limitation. Cut the construction immediately below its top level and fix the last cycle bit to zero. The other k−2 cycle bits yield 2^(k−2) distinct integral prefix assignments, although every crossing-edge value and both terminal inflows are identical. Consequently, any method that explicitly retains or enumerates every integral realization has exponential output even when those realizations are indistinguishable at the cut. A successful polynomial-time extension must merge such internal circulation choices or otherwise avoid representing them separately.

This is not an unrestricted computational lower bound. Indeed, the identical interface in the strengthened example shows exactly why compression remains possible. The fixed-supply boundary theorem also does not control the varying supply vectors induced by processed backward edges. No polynomial-size quotient, width-three ARRIVAL algorithm, or contrary complexity classification follows. The requested decision problem therefore remains open, and the claimed resolution is PARTIAL.
